avalanche.travel_advice: Watch for signs of unstable snow such as recent avalanches, cracking in the snow, and audible collapsing. Avoid traveling on or under similar slopes.

facts: No new snow measured at the 3 nearby stations in the 72 hours to Sep 28.

facts.text: Snow left Cascade Summit (5,100 ft) and Salt Creek Falls (4,220 ft) 36 to 42 days earlier this year than the median of the three earlier seasons on file (2023 to 2025).

evidence.name: Cascade Summit
evidence.detail: left April 23; earlier seasons: May 31 (2023), May 29 (2024), May 28 (2025)

evidence.name: Salt Creek Falls
evidence.detail: left April 4; earlier seasons: May 25 (2023), May 16 (2024), May 7 (2025)

facts.text: This year's highest snow water on or after April 1 was the lowest of the four seasons on file (2023 to 2026) at Cascade Summit (5,100 ft) and Salt Creek Falls (4,220 ft).

evidence.name: Cascade Summit
evidence.detail: 5.1 in on April 2; earlier seasons: 43.7 in (2023), 33.8 in (2024), 43.2 in (2025)

evidence.name: Salt Creek Falls
evidence.detail: 1.1 in on April 16; earlier seasons: 35.5 in (2023), 20.8 in (2024), 20.0 in (2025)

facts.text: An estimate: snow left the pass itself between March 26 and May 15, carried from the melt-out dates at Cascade Summit (5,100 ft) and Salt Creek Falls (4,220 ft) to the pass elevation.

evidence.name: Cascade Summit
evidence.detail: melted out April 23, 80 ft above the pass; points to March 31 to May 14

evidence.name: Salt Creek Falls
evidence.detail: melted out April 4, 800 ft below the pass; points to March 22 to May 15
